Theme 058 · Signature directions

Hand-Drawn Marker

Marker and pencil on warm dotted paper. The rule is strict: scribbles belong to the problem — red rings, crossed-out chores, a looping arrow, a highlighter smear — and an eraser wipes them all away on the drop. From then on the UI stays clean; only neat single-stroke teal ticks and one coral ring around the anomaly survive.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Dotted paper — warm off-white with a 30 px dot grid; the eraser leaves a dot-free band
  • Red marker ring — double overshooting ellipse around the one number that matters
  • Strike-through + loop arrow — marker lines over chores and an arrow that loops back to the start
  • Highlighter smear — amber at 40 %, ragged ends, under the active item
  • Sketch → real seam — pencil dashed wireframe that becomes crisp UI as a vertical seam passes
  • Sticky note + tape — peach note, 5° tilt, teal tape; carries the agent’s one-line suggestion

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Stroke draw — SVG stroke-dashoffset 100 → 0 over 0.3–0.5 s, power1.inOut, with a 1–2 px jitter pass for hand feel
  • Eraser wipe — mask rect scaleX 0 → 1 in exactly one beat (0.5 s at 120 BPM), linear, landing on the drop
  • Sticky slap — rotate 12° → 5°, scale 1.1 → 1, back.out(2) 0.25 s on a downbeat, plus a 2-frame shadow squash

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Hand marks feel human and honest, and the rule “mess = problem, clean = product” makes the before/after legible without words. Risk: too much scribble reads as childish or chaotic — cap the marks per frame and keep all numbers in clean type.

Adapt to your product: Scribble over your users’ current manual process in the hook, erase it on the drop, and let your real UI appear through a sketch→real seam; keep exactly one marker ring for the moment your product catches something.
